title: How much of the world's energy still comes from fossil fuels?
subtitle: Two hosts argue over the fossil slice of the world's energy pie, then find why it has barely shrunk since 1990 even as solar power boomed.
form: ask on pie slice (drag the edge)
notes: OWID's current chart (Energy Institute data released 2026, which includes 2025; 'share of total energy supply'): 86.2% in 2025, 90.3% in 1990. OWID's older substitution-method series gave ~81%; the source entry says which is used. Fix round: the template pie is drawn at full size for the guess, then replaced by two freehand pies side by side (1990 small, 2025 large, radius ∝ √ of total energy, ×1.81), year labels on each, '+73% fossil' arrow between; a gives the solar ×85 number, b reacts. Template 'animate box' does not resize a pie; a boxed pie with long slice names shrinks to a tiny disc.
